avoid.product_type: Apple-branded products (AirPods, iPad, Apple Watch, AirTag, EarPods)
avoid.reason: Heavily branded Apple products cannot be dropshipped — authorized reseller requirements, MAP pricing enforcement, and zero margin potential make every Apple bestseller on this list irrelevant for dropshippers. Do not attempt to source or resell.

avoid.product_type: Amazon-branded streaming and subscription devices (Fire TV Stick, Echo Dot, Kindle, Blink plans)
avoid.reason: Amazon private-label electronics (Fire TV, Echo, Kindle) are proprietary devices with no third-party dropship opportunity and are often sold at or below cost as ecosystem lock-in tools — margin is structurally impossible.

avoid.product_type: Replacement remote controls for specific TV brands (Roku, TCL, Hisense-compatible remotes)
avoid.reason: While showing Amazon demand, TV remotes are dominated by cheap private-label listings already at the lowest price floor ($8–$15), margin is razor-thin, and compatibility claims create high return rates that erode profitability.

avoid.product_type: Basic commodity bed sheet sets under $25 retail
avoid.reason: The queen sheet set category is aggressively price-competed to the point where landed costs from manufacturers leave under 15% margin after shipping — oversized, heavy packaging also increases fulfillment costs and damage rates significantly.

avoid.product_type: Oversized streaming and smart home hub devices requiring setup support
avoid.reason: Products like streaming sticks and smart speakers generate high customer service inquiries, have low retail prices relative to shipping weight, and are dominated by Amazon's own brand ecosystem — customer returns and compatibility issues are disproportionately high for dropshippers.

analysis.market_insights:
Late May 2026 presents a compelling seasonal entry window driven by three converging demand waves: pest control (ant, fly, and mosquito products simultaneously peaking), summer outdoor preparation (fans, cooling accessories, garden products), and the beginning of the summer travel and dorm prep cycle. Dropshippers who stock lightweight, consumable, or visually demonstrable products priced $20–$55 are well-positioned to capitalize on 6–10 weeks of elevated demand. The pest control window in particular is extremely time-sensitive — this category's demand curve is steep and narrow, typically collapsing by mid-August. The electronics accessories and drinkware categories offer more durable runway through Q3.

The absence of TikTok-specific viral data in today's dataset means some social commerce signals are inferred from Amazon rank patterns and category dynamics rather than confirmed view counts — this warrants caution on social-dependent products. However, the Amazon data alone is actionable: when 3+ products from the same category occupy simultaneous top-10 slots, category momentum is confirmed regardless of social data. The strongest risk-adjusted plays right now are surge protectors (evergreen), insulated water bottles (evergreen with summer spike), pest control consumables (seasonal peak NOW), and LED power display TWS earbuds (low COGS, high virality). Avoid any product in the Apple or Amazon ecosystem — those bestseller positions are noise for dropshippers, not signals.
analysis.data_quality_note: Today's dataset contains only Amazon bestseller data for two categories (Electronics and Home & Kitchen) with no TikTok view counts, Google Trends queries, or Movers & Shakers data provided — all social and search signals have been inferred from category expertise and seasonal context, so confidence ratings reflect this data limitation.
